g10-history-uh9-t1.overview: Indigenous Knowledge sits inside Indigenous Knowledge and Heritages of Ethiopia. Indigenous knowledge and heritage define this final unit of Grade 10 History in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it explains indigenous knowledge, its role in development, and its main features. Then it presents indigenous conflict resolution, from the Afar Mada’a and Dagu to the Oromo Jaarsummaa. Next, it covers the Siinqee, the Gumaa, the Amhara Shimgelina, and the Sidama Luwa. Also it explains the meaning and values of heritage. Finally, it lists Ethiopia’s natural, tangible, and intangible heritages. Students will also learn how indigenous knowledge applies to real-life situations, such as justice and unity in communities today.
objectives: Explain indigenous knowledge and its role in development.
Describe the main features of indigenous knowledge.
Compare the indigenous conflict resolution systems of Ethiopia.
Distinguish tangible from intangible heritage.
Evaluate the effectiveness of indigenous conflict resolution.
g10-history-uh9-t1.simple:
Indigenous Knowledge in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, indigenous knowledge as local wisdom passed down by oral tradition.
  • Its role in agriculture, health, food security, and resource management.
  • Also its features: simple, practical, and rooted in local language and culture.
g10-history-uh9-t1.detailed:
Indigenous Knowledge — the essentials. First, indigenous knowledge as local wisdom passed down by oral tradition. Its role in agriculture, health, food security, and resource management. Also its features: simple, practical, and rooted in local language and culture.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Explain indigenous knowledge and its role in development.
  • Describe the main features of indigenous knowledge.
  • Compare the indigenous conflict resolution systems of Ethiopia.
  • Distinguish tangible from intangible heritage.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of indigenous conflict resolution.
